evals.prompt: Regenerate the specs — I renamed the billing module to payments and deleted the old legacy-invoicing package last week.
evals.expected_output: Working tree is confirmed clean before anything else. The payments domain is generated fresh (or updated) by reading current source. The stale legacy-invoicing spec document is deleted from memory-bank/knowledge/specs/ as an orphan, since its corresponding code no longer exists. index.md is rewritten to reflect the new domain set. No file outside memory-bank/knowledge/specs/ is touched, and no document is deleted unless its orphan status is certain.
assertions: git status --porcelain is checked before any write/delete, and generation halts with the exact required error message if the tree isn't clean
The legacy-invoicing spec document is deleted only after confirming no corresponding code exists
No spec document is deleted outside the flat specs/ directory
index.md is rewritten and carries no frontmatter

evals.prompt: Regenerate specs for the whole repo. One existing doc, specs/legacy-scheduler.md, doesn't clearly map to any current directory — the code might have been moved rather than deleted, I'm not sure.
evals.expected_output: The ambiguous document is left in place rather than deleted, and is reported as an ambiguous/retained domain in the summary rather than silently skipped or silently removed.
assertions: The closing summary explicitly lists it as ambiguous/retained, not just absent from the deleted-orphans list

evals.prompt: Regenerate the specs — there are some uncommitted edits in the working tree from earlier today that I haven't committed yet.
evals.expected_output: The skill fails fast with 'spec requires a clean working tree. Commit or stash first.' before generating, deleting, or writing any specification document.
assertions: No spec document is generated, deleted, or written before the clean-tree check fails
The exact required error message is used, not a paraphrase
